strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear diagnosis of existing methods' limitations (task hallucinations in OS-Genesis, trajectory noise in Explorer) supported by concrete evidence (68.3% budget exceedance for Explorer vs. 0% for SynthAgent)
Principled dual-refinement strategy elegantly addressing the tension between task grounding and trajectory noise, with synergistic relationship well-articulated and justified

Comprehensive experimental validation across two complementary benchmarks (WebArena: controlled; Online-Mind2Web: 136 realistic websites) with multiple independent judges (GPT-4.1, GPT-5.1, Qwen3-30B)
Strong empirical results with consistent improvements (+10.2 over base model, +5.1 over OS-Genesis on WebArena; competitive with GPT-4.1 on Online-Mind2Web)
Thorough ablation studies quantifying component contributions, showing task refinement has largest impact (4.87% drop when removed)
Robust categorized exploration showing stable consistency (6-7.8 elements per category) across diverse website structures
Detailed analysis including t-SNE visualization of task diversity, trajectory completion rate breakdown, and scaling behavior with data amounts
Conservative trajectory refinement design (4.1% reordering operations, gated by independence checks) prioritizes safety while improving quality
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (categorized exploration, task refinement during execution, trajectory post-processing) are not novel; contribution is primarily in engineering their combination rather than introducing new techniques

Heavy dependence on GPT-4.1 for all synthesis and refinement operations limits reproducibility and practical accessibility; no ablation with alternative LLMs for synthesis (only for agent fine-tuning)

Underspecified design choices: conflict detection predicate (ExistsUI, MissingArgs, Stall) lacks formal justification; context window size (3) not empirically justified; refinement principles stated without rigorous analysis
Evaluation relies on LLM-as-judge with substantial variation across judges (trajectory quality ranges 75.0-92.5 in Tables 10-11); no human validation that trajectories are executable
WebArena evaluation uses restricted subset (226 of 812 tasks) due to computational constraints and excludes cross-website navigation; threatens generalizability claims

Fairness concerns in baseline comparison: Explorer re-implementation adds authentication support (absent in original), potentially affecting fair comparison; Explorer's surprisingly poor performance not fully explained

Limited scope: only evaluated on web navigation; unclear if approach generalizes to mobile apps, desktop GUIs, or other interactive environments; method leverages web-specific concepts (accessibility trees, DOM)
Incomplete ablation analysis: complex interaction between task and trajectory refinement under-explored (e.g., w/o TR&JR improves on Shopping but degrades on Maps without explanation)
No comparison with recent RL-based agent training approaches mentioned in related work (Lu et al., 2025; Qiu et al., 2025); limited discussion of cost-benefit versus human annotation scaling

strengths: Well-motivated design insight: Elegantly resolves the tension between environment grounding and trajectory noise through synergistic dual refinement strategy
Methodologically sound approach: Categorized exploration, conflict-triggered task refinement (Eq. 1), and conservative trajectory refinement are well-justified design choices

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Dual benchmarks (WebArena and Online-Mind2Web), proper baseline re-implementations, thorough ablations (Table 5), data quality analysis with t-SNE visualizations

Strong empirical results: Consistent improvements across benchmarks (+10.2 vs. base, +5.1 vs. OS-Genesis on WebArena), competitive with GPT-4.1 on Online-Mind2Web, highest task diversity and trajectory quality scores
Detailed baseline analysis: Convincing explanation of why Explorer underperforms (68.3% budget exceedance vs. 0% for SynthAgent) supported by trajectory statistics and proper re-implementation
Excellent reproducibility and clarity: Code publicly available, extensive implementation details in appendices, effective case studies (Figures 5-6) illustrating refinement process
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective motivation (Figure 1) and comprehensive supporting analysis
weaknesses: Heavy dependence on GPT-4.1 without thorough analysis: All synthesis, refinement, and post-processing rely on GPT-4.1 prompts; no cost-benefit analysis, comparison with other LLMs, or sensitivity analysis of prompt variations

Limited novelty in individual components: Categorized exploration largely adopts existing prompts from OS-Genesis; task refinement during execution is not new (Explorer does this); trajectory refinement is standard LLM-based post-processing. Primary contribution is pipeline design (incremental relative to Explorer)

Evaluation fairness concerns: SFT upper bound trains on full 812 WebArena tasks while synthetic methods train on ≤500 per website, making comparison unfair; Online-Mind2Web uses LLM-as-Judge without inter-rater agreement or confidence intervals

Task refinement predicates are heuristic-based without sensitivity analysis: ExistsUI and MissingArgs detection are underspecified; Stall uses fixed thresholds (3 no-ops, same loop twice) with no robustness analysis or failure mode discussion

Limited statistical rigor: No significance testing, error bars, or confidence intervals reported; high variance across websites (Maps 28.12 vs. Reddit 15.38) not analyzed; per-website ablations missing

Limited scope and generalization claims: WebArena has only 5 websites; generalization to completely novel websites not demonstrated (Online-Mind2Web trains on mixed data from other sites); no analysis of which tasks/websites benefit most or cause failures

Incomplete failure analysis: Only 0.4% trajectory drop rate but no investigation of why these fail; trajectory reordering provides only modest gains on small sample (42% vs. 27% win rate on 100 trajectories); no qualitative negative case studies
